sanskrit: ūrdhvaśrito vai nāmaitā āpo yad oṣadhayaś ca vanaspatayaś ca tāsām agnir adhipatiḥ | yo vā etā ūrdhvaśrita āpo vedāgnim adhipatim | yathaitam etā ūrdhvā upatiṣṭhanty evainam ūrdhvā upa tiṣṭhanty adhipatir bhavati svānāṃ cānyeṣāṃ ca ya evaṃ veda ||
english: Those waters that are herbs and forest-trees — verily those are called the Upward-Standing (ūrdhvaśritāḥ); Agni is their overlord. Whoso knows these Upward-Standing waters, knowing Agni as their overlord — even as those waters stand upright before him, so do they stand upright before this knower; he becomes overlord among his own people and among others — he who knows thus.

sanskrit: praskadvarīr vai nāmaitā āpo yat pṛṣvās tāsām ādityo 'dhipatiḥ | yo vā etāḥ praskadvarīr āpo vedādityam adhipatim | yathaitā etasminn udyati praskandanty evāsminn ā yati praskandanty adhipatiḥ (…) ||
english: Those waters that are the dew-drops (pṛṣvāḥ) — verily those are called the Leaping-Forth (praskadvarīḥ); Āditya is their overlord. Whoso knows these Leaping-Forth waters, knowing Āditya as their overlord — even as they leap forth when he rises and leap forth when he comes back, so does he become overlord [among his own and among others, he who knows thus].

sanskrit: takvarīr vai nāmaitā āpo yāḥ sūdaya tāsāṃ pṛthivy adhipatnī | yo vā etās takvarīr āpo veda pṛthivīm adhipatnīm | yathaitā etasyāṃ praṇutās takantīr yanty evainena dviṣantaḥ praṇutā yanty adhipatiḥ (…) ||
english: Those waters that flow in channels (sūdayāḥ) — verily those are called the Swift-Running (takvarīḥ); Pṛthivī is their overlord. Whoso knows these Swift-Running waters, knowing Pṛthivī as their overlord — even as those waters, when driven forth upon her, run swiftly away, so are his enemies driven forth and run away; he becomes overlord [among his own and among others, he who knows thus].

sanskrit: vaśinīr vai nāmaitā āpo yāḥ syandante tāsāṃ varuṇo 'dhipatiḥ | yo vā etā vaśinīr āpo veda varuṇam adhipatim | yathaitam etāsāṃ syandamānānāṃ vaśam ādatta evā dviṣatāṃ vaśam ā datte 'dhipatiḥ (…) ||
english: Those waters that glide in streams (syandante) — verily those are called the Obedient (vaśinīḥ); Varuṇa is their overlord. Whoso knows these Obedient waters, knowing Varuṇa as their overlord — even as he takes those streaming waters under his will, so does he take his foes under his will; he becomes overlord [among his own and among others, he who knows thus].

sanskrit: ūrjo vai nāmaitā āpo yad gāvas tāsāṃ tvaṣṭādhipatiḥ | yo vā etā ūrja āpo veda tvaṣṭāram adhipatim | ūrjasvī tejasvī bhavati pra sāhasrān paśūn āpnoty adhipatiḥ (…) ||
english: Those waters that are cows — verily those are called the Vigour-Waters (ūrjāḥ); Tvaṣṭṛ is their overlord. Whoso knows these Vigour-Waters, knowing Tvaṣṭṛ as their overlord — he becomes rich in vigour, radiant with splendour; he gains cattle by the thousand; he becomes overlord [among his own and among others, he who knows thus].

sanskrit: varco vai nāmaitā āpo yad ghṛtaṃ tāsāṃ pūṣā adhipatiḥ | yo vā etā varca āpo veda pūṣaṇam adhipatim | varcasvī tejasvī bhavaty utāsyānabhyaktasya mukhaṃ rocate 'dhipatiḥ (…) ||
english: Those waters that are clarified butter (ghṛta) — verily those are called the Lustre-Waters (varcāḥ); Pūṣan is their overlord. Whoso knows these Lustre-Waters, knowing Pūṣan as their overlord — he becomes lustrous and radiant with splendour; and even the face of this one, though unanointed, shines bright; he becomes overlord [among his own and among others, he who knows thus].

sanskrit: ojo vai nāmaitā āpo yan madhu tāsām indro 'dhipatiḥ | yo vā etā oja āpo vedendram adhipatim | ojasvī vīryāvān indriyāvī bhavati pra rājasabhāyāṃ madhuparkam āpnoty adhipatiḥ (…) ||
english: Those waters that are honey (madhu) — verily those are called the Might-Waters (ojāḥ); Indra is their overlord. Whoso knows these Might-Waters, knowing Indra as their overlord — he becomes mighty, heroic, possessed of vital force; he obtains the honey-mixture (madhuparka) in the royal assembly; he becomes overlord [among his own and among others, he who knows thus].

sanskrit: ugrā vai nāmaitā āpo yad dhrādunayas tāsāṃ maruto adhipatayaḥ | yo vā etā ugrā āpo veda maruto 'dhipatīn | ugro balavāna bhavati mārutaṃ śardha ity enam āhur adhipatiḥ (…) ||
english: Those waters that are the hailstones (dhrādunayaḥ) — verily those are called the Fierce-Waters (ugrāḥ); the Maruts are their overlords. Whoso knows these Fierce-Waters, knowing the Maruts as their overlords — he becomes fierce and powerful; people call him 'the host of Maruts (mārutaṃ śardhaḥ)'; he becomes overlord [among his own and among others, he who knows thus].

sanskrit: maho vai nāmaitā āpo yad varṣaṃ tāsāṃ parjanyo 'dhipatiḥ | yo vā etā maha āpo veda parjanyam adhipatim | mahasvī mitrabāho bhavaty utainena svā nandanty asmākam ayam iti tasmāt sarvo vṛṣṭe mahīyate 'dhipatiḥ (…) ||
english: Those waters that are rain (varṣa) — verily those are called the Great-Waters (mahāḥ); Parjanya is their overlord. Whoso knows these Great-Waters, knowing Parjanya as their overlord — he becomes great, with far-reaching friendship; his own people rejoice in him, saying 'He is ours.' Therefore everyone exults at rain; he becomes overlord [among his own and among others, he who knows thus].

sanskrit: atimanyā vai nāmaitā āpo yat surā tasām aśvinādhipatī | yo vā etā atimanyā āpo vedāśvinādhipatī | ati manyate bhrātṛvyān nainaṃ bhrātṛvyā ati manyante tasmān matto mattam ati manyate 'dhipatiḥ (…) ||
english: Those waters that are spirituous liquor (surā) — verily those are called the Exceedingly-Proud (atimanyāḥ); the two Aśvins are their overlords. Whoso knows these Exceedingly-Proud waters, knowing the two Aśvins as their overlords — he is prouder than his rivals; his rivals are not prouder than he. That is why an intoxicated man is prouder than another intoxicated man; he becomes overlord [among his own and among others, he who knows thus].

sanskrit: paricito vai nāmaitā āpo yāḥ karṣvāṃ tāsāṃ yamo 'dhipatiḥ | yo vā etāḥ paricita āpo veda yamam adhipatim | pary enaṃ svāś ca viśyāś ca avaśyanty adhipatiḥ (…) ||
english: Those waters that flow in furrows (karṣvāḥ) — verily those are called the Gathered-Round (paricitāḥ); Yama is their overlord. Whoso knows these Gathered-Round waters, knowing Yama as their overlord — both his own kinsmen and his clansmen gather around him in submission; he becomes overlord [among his own and among others, he who knows thus].

sanskrit: rantayo vai nāmaitā āpo ya striyas tāsāṃ kāmo 'dhipatiḥ | yo vā etā rantīr āpo veda kāmam adhipatim | ramante asmin ramaṇīyo bhavati kāma iva strīṇām adhipatiḥ (…) ||
english: Those waters that are women (striyaḥ) — verily those are called the Delightful-Waters (rantayaḥ); Kāma is their overlord. Whoso knows these Delightful-Waters, knowing Kāma as their overlord — people take pleasure in him; he becomes delightful, as Kāma is overlord among women; he becomes overlord [among his own and among others, he who knows thus].

sanskrit: viśvabhṛto vai nāmaitā āpo yat puruṣas tāsāṃ mṛtyur adhipatiḥ | yo vā etā viśvabhṛta āpo veda mṛtyum adhipatim | viśvasya bhartā bhavati viśvam enaṃ bibharty āsya trayo 'gnayo gṛhe dhīyante dakṣiṇāgnir gārhapatya āhavanīyaḥ | ainaṃ catvāri vāmāni gacchanti niṣkaḥ kaṃso 'śvataro hasty adhipatiḥ (…) ||
english: Those waters that are the human person (puruṣa) — verily those are called the All-Sustaining (viśvabhṛtāḥ); Mṛtyu is their overlord. Whoso knows these All-Sustaining waters, knowing Mṛtyu as their overlord — he becomes the sustainer of all; all sustain him. In his house the three sacrificial fires are established: the Dakṣiṇāgni, the Gārhapatya, and the Āhavanīya. And four auspicious gifts come to him: the golden necklace (niṣka), the bowl (kaṃsa), the mule (aśvatara), and the elephant; he becomes overlord [among his own and among others, he who knows thus].

sanskrit: tāsāṃ vā etāsām apāṃ himavān ūdhaḥ somo vatsaḥ parameṣṭhy adhipatiḥ | yo vā etāsām apāṃ himavantam ūdhaḥ somaṃ vatsaṃ parameṣṭhinam adhipatiṃ veda | parameṣṭhī bhavati gacchati parameṣṭhitām adhipatiḥ bhavati svānāṃ cānyeṣāṃ ca ya evaṃ veda ||
english: Of all these waters, the Himālaya is their udder, Soma is their calf, and Parameṣṭhin is their overlord. Whoso knows of these waters that the Himālaya is their udder, Soma their calf, and Parameṣṭhin their overlord — he becomes Parameṣṭhin, he attains the state of supreme sovereignty; he becomes overlord among his own people and among others — he who knows thus.
